matches.label: equivalent
matches.rationale: Creator and author of a dataset are close synonyms, so this is the same information item for the same resource.

matches.label: partial
matches.rationale: A methods narrative overlaps a lineage description, but the need covers descriptions in general (abstract, methods, technical information) rather than lineage as such.

matches.label: partial
matches.rationale: Typed relations such as derivation links express part of a lineage, but the need is a general relation mechanism for any resource.

matches.label: partial
matches.rationale: Explanatory and technical descriptions can carry guidance on use, but the need is not specifically about how to use the data and also covers methods.

matches.label: broader
matches.rationale: Typed relationships from a resource to related objects include links from a dataset to publications about it, among other relations.

matches.label: broader
matches.rationale: Typed relationships to related objects include a link from a dataset to the data it was derived from, among other relations.

matches.label: partial
matches.rationale: The catalogue publisher's identifier given as a URI is one case of URI-encoded identifiers, but the need covers only that identifier and does not ask for HTTP URIs generally.

matches.label: partial
matches.rationale: It separates alternative identifiers from the primary DOI, but it fixes the primary identifier to a DOI and adds identifier types.

matches.label: partial
matches.rationale: It presupposes that the dataset's primary identifier is a DOI, but it asks for the other identifiers and their types and has no DataCite-citation condition.

matches.label: narrower
matches.rationale: Identifier types for a dataset's non-primary identifiers are a special case of qualifying each identifier with its type.

matches.label: partial
matches.rationale: Typed contributor roles such as curation go beyond publisher and contact point, but the need also includes contact roles and does not ask for a minimal, unambiguous role set.

matches.label: partial
matches.rationale: Curation roles are one kind of agent role beyond publisher and contact point, but the need does not ask for a minimal, consistent role set.

matches.label: partial
matches.rationale: Same role-typing item, but for contact roles, which the atom places outside its scope, and without a minimal role set.

matches.label: partial
matches.rationale: Knowing the interfaces through which data are accessed overlaps flagging service/API access, but it is a general statement about JRC data, not a per-distribution indication.

matches.label: partial
matches.rationale: Knowing which interfaces give access overlaps describing the API, but the need asks for no interface description or query parameters and does not target software agents.

matches.label: partial
matches.rationale: A methods narrative is part of provenance and helps reproducibility, but the need does not ask for detailed provenance or usage tracking.

matches.label: partial
matches.rationale: Typed relations such as derivation or citation links carry some provenance and usage information, but the need is a general relation mechanism without reproducibility-level detail.
